intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 24 October 2026 featured three shifts with varying difficulty levels. Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, with unofficial good‑attempt figures ranging between 70 and 85. Shift 2 leaned towards moderate‑to‑difficult, with unofficial good‑attempt figures between 62 and 72. Shift 3 was described as easy, but its good‑attempt numbers are not reliably reported, and only a limited review is available pending further corroboration. All figures are unofficial and the SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level for each shift on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, Shift 2 as moderate to difficult, and Shift 3 as easy according to the majority of candidate reports.

faqs.q: How did candidates perform in terms of good attempts for the reported shifts on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: For Shift 1, candidates reported good attempts between 70 and 85 questions. For Shift 2, the range was between 62 and 72 questions. No reliable good‑attempt data is available for Shift 3.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as most challenging on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, the Quantitative Aptitude section was noted as the toughest, while General Awareness varied in difficulty. In Shift 2, Quantitative Aptitude leaned towards difficult and Reasoning and General Awareness were moderate to difficult. In Shift 3, Reasoning was easy but time‑consuming, and some candidates could not finish all questions.

faqs.q: Is there any analysis available for Shift 3 on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: A limited review for Shift 3 has been published, describing it as easy overall, but the analysis needs further corroboration before it can be considered comprehensive.

faqs.q: Are the reported figures for the 24 October 2026 exam official?
faqs.a: No. The figures presented are unofficial; the SSC normalises scores across shifts, and official statistics have not been released.
